newsitem.title: GERMANY: France's Trichet expects deficit-cutting budget.
newsitem.headline: France's Trichet expects deficit-cutting budget.

text.p: Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Tuesday the central bank expected the government's 1997 budget, to be announced on Wednesday, to conform with its already announced deficit reduction strategy.
"The council of monetary policy is expecting we will proceed along the strategy which has been floated already and is absolutely key for confidence," he told Reuters Financial Television.

That strategy, he said, involved cutting the French public deficit to five percent of gross domestic product in 1995, four percent in 1996 and three percent in 1997 to qualify for European monetary union.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis's budget is expected to hold spending for next year at 1996 levels in the drive to reduce the deficit.
Trichet was speaking after a Franco-German economic meeting.
The central bank governor, asked whether the budget could pave the way for further monetary easing, declined to comment.
But, he added, "You have to consider that already the Bank of France and the money markets on the other hand have delivered very low market rates."
"There you can see we have improved confidence a lot," he said, adding that appropriate fiscal policy and monetary stability was important to the Bank of France.
